articles.title: Live updates: Trump, Vance to close out RNC midterm convention; Democrats counter with protests
articles.summary: Vice President Vance will take his turn at the Republican National Committee midterm convention podium Thursday night, followed by President Trump, as GOP members close out their two-day push to energize voters ahead of November’s midterms. Trump spoke for over 90 minutes on Wednesday night, urging voters to cast a ballot as though he were…
articles.body:
Vice President Vance will take his turn at the Republican National Committee midterm convention podium Thursday night, followed by President Trump, as GOP members close out their two-day push to energize voters ahead of November’s midterms.

Trump spoke for over 90 minutes on Wednesday night, urging voters to cast a ballot as though he were running.

“I mean, we’re running together,” the president said, as he capped off the convention’s first night. “We have to have Congress. We have to have the majorities. If we don’t have the majorities, so much can be lost.”

Trump went on to offer up a $5,000 dividend incentive to every American adult if his party keeps Democrats from taking back the House this fall. He called them “Trump dividends” and said they had to be spent in the U.S.

Vance did not appear on the event’s first night. The convention will lean heavily on the president’s inner circle for Day Two — with his son, Donald Trump Jr., former press secretary Karoline Leavitt and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. all slated to speak.

Other notable speakers include House Speaker Mike Johnson (La.), Sen. Ted Cruz (Texas) and Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, who’s seeking reelection.

Also on the RNC’s agenda is a tribute to slain conservative activist Charlie Kirk in honor of the one-year anniversary of his death. Kirk’s youth organization, Turning Point USA, is holding a memorial Thursday night at Utah Valley University — where he was fatally shot during an on-campus speaker event in front of thousands of attendees.

Meanwhile, Democrats have planned a march protesting the convention, meeting at Dallas City Hall Plaza, as they also did the day prior. The rally is scheduled for 2 p.m. EDT.

In Missouri, Secretary of State Denny Hoskins (R) is set to appear before the state Supreme Court on Thursday as judges weigh whether to hold him in contempt amid an escalating battle over the state’s congressional map .

articles.title: Democratic socialist backed by Bernie Sanders ousts Providence, Rhode Island mayor
articles.summary: Rhode Island Rep. David Morales, 27, defeated Providence Mayor Brett Smiley by 8 points after campaigning on rent stabilization and housing justice.
articles.body: Rhode Island State Rep. David Morales, a 27-year-old democratic socialist endorsed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., defeated Providence Mayor Brett Smiley in the Democratic primary Wednesday night, ousting the incumbent after one term. If Morales wins the general election, he will be Providence's youngest mayor in history. "Few believed that a 27-year-old democratic socialist could ever, few believed that we could ever take on big money, corporate real estate interests and endless attack ads – and we took them on and we won," Morales said in his victory speech, delivered partly in Spanish, after winning by roughly 8 points (54%-46%). Smiley, 47, who faced his heaviest media scrutiny over his handling of the Brown University shooting last December, served just one term. AMERICA’S QUIET SOCIALIST TAKEOVER IS SPREADING FROM TOWN HALLS TO CLASSROOMS "So neighbors, with the bold agenda and the mandate that we have voted for, let's get ready. Providence, let's get ready." Morales will face Republican nominee Dave Talan, 77, in November. Republicans hold no seats on the Providence City Council, and Democrats make up a majority of registered voters in the city. Former Vice President Kamala Harris beat President Donald Trump in the city by 51 points in 2024. "The voters of Providence made their choice, and they chose David Morales as our next mayor in the Democratic primary," Smiley said in his concession speech after calling Morales. "While I’m not happy with that outcome, I’m so happy and proud of the campaign that we ran." STATE OF PLAY: WHAT TO KNOW ABOUT POTENTIAL SOCIALIST SHOWDOWN BETWEEN TRUMP AND DC MAYOR AS VOTES POUR IN Morales, who also received backing from Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., former Providence Mayor Jorge Elorza and several labor unions, campaigned on a progressive platform that included capping rent hikes, expanding affordable housing and raising taxes on polluters and corporate landlords. "Nearly a year ago today, we launched a campaign centered around a simple vision that the working people who make Providence home deserve to live here," Morales said. "A simple vision that our neighbors deserve a mayor who will fight for them." The contest was part of a broader series of Democratic primary battles between progressive challengers and more established incumbents. Morales sought to tap into frustration over housing costs and the direction of city government, while Smiley argued that his experience and record made him the better choice to lead Providence. SOCIALIST INSURGENTS FORCE MODERATE DEMOCRATS INTO HIGH-RISK SHOWDOWN OVER MUST-HOLD RACES "The same way that we campaigned, we are going to govern — in coalition, side by side with our neighbors," Morales said. The primary also featured a battle over rent stabilization. The Providence City Council approved a measure that would have capped annual rent increases at 4% for certain apartments, but Smiley vetoed it in April. The council fell one vote short of overriding the veto in May. MAMDANI’S AFFORDABILITY REVOLUTION STUMBLED AS RENT COSTS SOAR TO RECORD HIGHS "When working people are getting priced out of the city that they love, then we must cap rent increases at 4% every single year," Morales said. "We put housing justice on the ballot." Morales also ran as a hard-liner on Providence being a sanctuary for illegal migrants, and against the Trump administration's effort to enforce U.S. immigration law.
